title: Longitudinal Capacity Timeline and Deferred Resequencing Adapter
author: Priya Menon
description: This PR introduces a longitudinal capacity timeline subsystem and a deferred resequencing adapter to improve commitment application stability for Dedicated fleets. Motivation: we've observed oscillation when many overlapping reservations and decommits are applied in rapid succession, leading to ineffective warmups and spiky tail latency. The timeline records commitment events (reserve/adjust/release) with logical ordering and a windowed reconciliation pass that smooths immediate application, enabling the autoscaler to make informed steady-state decisions. The resequencing adapter defers application of high-frequency reservation deltas for tenants flagged as 'churn-prone' and replays them in an idempotent, coalesced form during quiet windows so we avoid repeated warm pool churn. Changes include a new timeline controller (redwood/fleet/timeline_controller.go) with unit + integration tests, a small DB migration to add capacity_timeline_events and a compacted_offset pointer, telemetry hooks that emit tenant_weekly_commitment_quantiles and timeline_replay_duration_ms, an autoscaler hook that consults the timeline's smoothed commitment rate before firing up additional capacity, and a CLI tool to inspect recent timeline windows (bin/rwctl timeline tail). The PR also adds a safety backstop that forces immediate application if replay is delayed beyond a configurable threshold to preserve correctness in corner cases. Implementation notes: event schema is intentionally compact and oriented to append-only semantics, replay is idempotent and safe under retries, the DB migration is backward compatible and guarded by a feature flag fleet.timeline_v1 which defaults to off for gradual rollout. Testing: included a deterministic simulation harness to reproduce the previously observed oscillation and a test scenario demonstrating >35% reduction in warm-pool churn under synthetic multi-tenant bursts. Deployment plan: feature gated rollout to 10% of Dedicated fleets in Canary followed by 100% after 48 hours of telemetry validation. See linked XS support ticket SUP-2109 for a customer incident that motivated this work.
commits_summary: 5 commits: add timeline controller and tests; add DB migration and feature flag wiring; implement deferred resequencing adapter and autoscaler hook; telemetry and rwctl CLI; docs and changelog updates.
review_thread: Evan: This looks promising. Two questions: 1) how does replay interact with concurrent manual decommits? 2) can we bound DB growth?

Priya: Answered inline. Replay checks event idempotency tokens and honors manual decommit flags; compacted_offset truncation meets retention policy and we added a daily compaction job. Also added explicit tests for manual decommit race.
Marco: Please add an integration test that runs with the feature flag off to ensure no regressions for fleets that don't enable timeline.
Priya: Added tests and updated migration to be a no-op when the flag is off. CI now runs the matrix with feature flag on/off.
Hannah: Telemetry naming looks good, but add an alert suggestion in docs for timeline_replay_duration_ms exceeding threshold.
Priya: Added alert guidance and a Grafana panel snippet in docs/observability/timeline.md
merge_outcome: squash and merge by Priya Menon after all reviewers approved. Rollout gated by feature flag fleet.timeline_v1 and coordinated with SRE runbook.
release_notes: Adds an optional longitudinal capacity timeline for Dedicated fleets that smooths high-frequency reservation churn and reduces warm-pool oscillation. Feature gated behind fleet.timeline_v1. Includes telemetry and CLI tooling for inspection.
notes_for_ops: Default rollout is disabled. To enable: set feature flag fleet.timeline_v1=true and run the migration migration/20260114_add_capacity_timeline.sql in the control-plane DB. Monitor tenant_weekly_commitment_quantiles and timeline_replay_duration_ms. If replay delay spikes, toggle feature off and contact oncall. There is a compact job that truncates old events; ensure retention settings are applied.
post_merge_actions: Apply DB migration to control-plane in Canary, enable feature flag for 10% of Dedicated fleets, monitor for 48h, then ramp to 100% if metrics stable. Coordinate with SRE for canary window.
customer_impact: reduces warm-pool churn and improves throughput stability for tenants with bursty reservation patterns
